# social-service-ea per-operation parity backlog

Baseline: `decentraland/social-service-ea@b6b2cefefdf727b2ed47ddb887e77d226a41eea6`. The machine source is [parity.json](parity.json).

The source inventory contains **123 operations**: 5 api_auxiliary, 72 api_http, 6 json_stream, 6 rpc_stream, 27 rpc_unary, 5 uws_http, 2 websocket.

reviewed means the stated source/behaviour scope was compared; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a remaining observed difference. not_reviewed requires an explicit comparison, even if a matching route or local test exists.

Source hashes include the pinned service registrations, handlers, stream definitions, lockfile and the installed framework code that supplies health, CORS, metrics and fallback handling. `tooling/social-service-parity.py --upstream <checkout>` re-derives that inventory; the default check validates its complete backlog, local evidence references and the 33-method protocol set and complete source-pinned social-service/error/color schema hashes without an external checkout. The only other schema import is the standard `google/protobuf/empty.proto`.

Executed upstream handler cases live in [source-cases.json](source-cases.json); their Protobuf bytes are replayed by `rpc_wire_answers_match_executed_upstream_source_cases`. Those cases use injected dependencies and do not prove deployed HTTP, Redis, SNS, PostgreSQL or live-client equivalence.

## Shared gaps and replacement requirements

These requirements remain open even when an operation's focused review passes. A local implementation or a matching fixture does not establish a completed cutover.

| Requirement | Status | Evidence and remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `external-notification-consumers` | unverified | Configured friendship and all twelve community SNS producers preserve source raw fields, keys and recipient policies through the existing official SDK publisher. Source/local stub tests cover 100-recipient pages/messages, ten-message requests, failure isolation, opt-out independence and HTTP background versus voice-awaited execution. Existing deployed topic subscriptions, downstream consumers, retry timing and migration/cutover delivery remain unverified. |
| `cross-replica-social-events` | unverified | Mutation fanout uses the existing core NATS link. Awaited publisher enqueue, synchronous targeted delivery and a 1,000-entry community work queue with at most min(4,pool size) SQL tasks deliver actual 1,000-update targeted/community bursts locally. Control traffic remains live; large public snapshots, process-local context restart and cache expiry are covered. Delivery remains transient and at most once. Deployed replica/consumer behavior, traffic beyond these measured bounds and outage/reconnect equivalence remain unverified. |
| `community-started-audience-lifetime` | unverified | Audience scope/generation/24-hour refreshed expiry now persist in shared SQL. Restart, expiry, generation-CAS and retained immutable event snapshots pass local tests. Existing room state, external media continuity and deployed cutover remain unverified. |
| `referral-lifecycle` | known_gap | Attribution/IP rejection, signup, UTC login days, guarded grants, artwork, email, handler-specific database errors and configured Slack effects have source-paired/local regressions and optional real SQS/SNS SDK transport. Slack retains the existing Outbound8s connect/25s read limits and host guard instead of the source SDK timeout0;16 executed numeric configurations cover source parser values, bigint rejection/overflow and login-day comparisons. Stateful deployed cutover remains unverified. |
| `community-ranking-and-configured-moderation` | known_gap | Dynamic moderators, ranking producers and configured AI compliance are implemented with focused source/local regressions. AI provider timeout/body bounds and missing-credential bootstrap behavior still differ. Existing lifetime counter baselines and watermarks are not imported, so historical ranking equality remains unverified. |
| `shared-fixed-window-friendship-limit` | unverified | The implemented SQL limiter now matches eight executed source/Redis scenarios plus concurrent replica, fixed-expiry and configuration regressions. Existing Redis counter state has not been imported or drained during a nonempty cutover; a fresh SQL counter resets the active window. |
| `cutover-with-existing-state` | unverified | No nonempty migration snapshot, deployed provider/edge configuration, active LiveKit call continuity, running-client comparison or rollback rehearsal has been supplied or executed. These are replacement acceptance requirements, separate from local contract tests. |
| `referral-external-cutover` | unverified | Configured official SQS/SNS transports preserve legacy raw events and attributes locally; ranking dispatch, friendship and community publication are wired. Deployed queue policies, topic subscriptions and credential access have not been exercised. Populated candidate additive upgrades pass synthetic tests; existing upstream progress/login-days/reward/email import and live cutover remain outstanding. |
| `api-body-size-boundary` | known_gap | Configured HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES uses source prefix parsing and integer 1..16MiB admission. Declared oversize rejects before routing/auth; deferred reads preserve schema400 versus raw/multipart500 and independent multipart1MiB/thumbnail1..500KiB limits. Eighteen boot and 44 HTTP body cases replay through real drain/Normalize. Gateway-only authentication now precedes mirror SQL and federation classification; client JSON uses its configured cap. Twelve additional actual-source server cases independently regenerate exactly, with eight healthy candidate exchanges and separate denied-role auth/SQL controls. Native aliases retain 1MiB fallback and buffer512KiB-before-auth federation contracts; confirmed gateway envelopes retain typed verification and512KiB cap after classification. Known differences remain: signed body-ignoring joins answer immediately in source but classification needs complete JSON, oversized incomplete envelopes can reject later, and unread fast chunked overflow uses different connection-close timing. Raw framing, longer transport lifetime and concurrent resource use remain unverified. |
| `shared-social-profile-cache` | unverified | RPC and community adapters share source 600-second SQL cache facts over the existing pool. Twenty-nine historical lookup steps, eight strict owner handler cases and eight mixed-case adapter steps pass source/local replay. Requested keys and Set deduplication preserve exact case; physical content-pointer lookup remains normalized. The mixed-case registry response is injected, so deployed registry case/order behavior is unverified. Existing Redis values and remaining TTL have not been imported or drained for cutover. |
| `community-dependency-error-boundaries` | unverified | All 37 community handlers now preserve source message-only 500 for unexpected core SQL errors. Independently recaptured actual Node handlers receive a real node-pg exception through injected domain dependencies; candidate requests exercise restricted-role PostgreSQL faults and paired standing failures. Author community suite passes 184 cases, including unchanged federation error envelopes. Registry-read/provider/voice failure phases remain separate requirements; arbitrary driver error wording and deployed outages are not proven equivalent. |
| `rpc-ordinary-transport-backpressure` | known_gap | The existing Social opt-in writer now bounds ordinary pending frames with the source adaptive count, retry/backoff/drain policy and accepted-once semantics. Fifteen supported-policy source traces replay; two additional cases document candidate startup rejection for maxBackpressure0 and computed nonfinite queue capacity where the source can admit unbounded buffering. WS_MAX_BACKPRESSURE still uses a strict unsigned parser rather than native numeric-prefix/fraction/wrap conversion. Application writer admission/flush is measured separately from native uWS kernel behavior; deployed performance equivalence is unverified. Twenty executed source backpressure-number cases now separate raw f64 queue capacity from native unsigned32 truncation/wrap. Prefix, fraction and representable wrap inputs are implemented; native-zero and nonfinite-capacity configurations remain unsupported and unaccepted, and kernel/performance equivalence remains unverified. |
| `community-voice-status-failure-degradation` | unverified | Core community SQL and voice reads now use separate queries on the same pool/config through existing VoiceDb methods. Companion voice SQL failures yield idle/empty, while core failures retain500; active filters return empty before core reads if their voice result is empty or failed. Twenty-nine actual-source component/handler/adapter cases cover companion SQL stages, core errors and direct-provider500; candidate regression pairs18 requests plus three dual-fault controls. Source errors are injected; target faults are real PostgreSQL permissions. Package community193/all-targets/module checks pass. Direct-provider transport, concurrent snapshots and deployed cutover remain unverified. Ordinary voice reads are bounded by returned page IDs; all-active scans remain global. |
| `social-client-artifact-cutover` | unverified | Signed Social paths now match 81 source verifier decisions and real socket replays. The Bevy client preserves its connection URL while signing /; a native cryptographic unit covers standalone, mounted and query URLs. Deployed web artifacts must contain that update before strict server cutover. Cached/running clients, full Explorer, wasm and rendered /play behavior have not been exercised. |
| `social-initial-subscription-readiness` | known_gap | The Social subscription is registered and retained before its first readiness latch observes the existing broker fence. Both valid upgrades are refused before auth/slots until that latch; later outages retain transient at-most-once policy. Six actual source lifecycle stages and two candidate tests cover order and local-mode admission. Candidate startup responds empty HTTP 503 while the standalone source listener is not yet open; this operational difference is explicit and has no user acceptance verdict. |
| `community-fanout-whole-membership-failure` | unverified | Pinned logic/updates.ts gathers every membership page before delivery. Candidate now snapshots eligible subscribers, completes all bounded 256-address probes before emitting, aborts all member-scoped delivery on any failed page and clears all isMember annotations on a failed public STARTED; public ENDED skips membership reads. Six independently recaptured actual-source cases and the owned-SQL second-page failure regression pass, including 513 eligible recipients and zero partial emissions. All seven fanout tests pass, including actual NATS. Fresh independent static review confirms the whole-audience fix; deployed failure behavior and final aggregate review remain unverified. |
| `configured-social-analytics-effects` | known_gap | All 16 source analytics event kinds are connected at the 17 voice/community producer sites through the shared concrete adapter. Source captures cover 35 voice scenarios and 19 community scenarios; candidate regressions pair all 35 voice and 17 normal/no-op community scenarios, with nine separately paired PostgreSQL trigger cases for partial-write boundaries. Source SDK configuration, response cancellation, cross-host redirects and whole-chain deadlines are independently recaptured. Known unaccepted transport differences remain: shared connect8s/read25s, host guarding and optional monolith startup when all analytics strings are absent. Deployed routing/provider behavior and transient-event cutover remain unverified. The six entry-wrapper cases preserve raw RPC recipient and HTTP private-call identifier spellings independently from normalized SQL/authorization/recipient keys. |
| `private-call-pending-expiry-start-order` | unverified | Pending calls now keep both parties busy until the expiry sweep deletes them; starting a call never reclaims expired pending rows or emits their EXPIRED event. All 35 voice analytics/source scenarios are now paired, including the expired-start case. Voice package 56 tests and comms voice-database seven tests pass. Production sweep timing and existing-state cutover remain unverified. |
| `private-call-disconnect-accepted-media` | unverified | Social disconnect now finishes only pending calls. An accepted row, its two participants and media room remain until explicit media end; the owned-PostgreSQL regression and source domain captures match. Package voice 56 tests pass. Live clients and media-room cutover remain unverified. |
| `community-registry-read-failure-propagation` | unverified | The six V1 profile-enriched reads now propagate existing registry batch read errors while cache writes remain best effort and V2 controls do not fetch profiles. Eighteen actual-source cases independently regenerate exactly; all18 target PostgreSQL permission-fault/control exchanges and the existing normal profile-source regression pass at root. Package community192, all-targets and module checks pass. Missing-profile row semantics, other dependency failures, deployed cache state and cutover remain separate verification. |
| `private-call-stale-media-coexistence` | unverified | Actual Social/companion PostgreSQL components and the candidate now permit a new pending call when retained media presence is initial-expired, interrupted-expired or disconnected. Six lifecycle cases and two media-writer sequences are independently recaptured exactly. Candidate credentials retain older pending/media rows; actual join and explicit end own cleanup by call identity. Explicit READ COMMITTED and ordered normalized-wallet locks preserve one pending across roles under a REPEATABLE READ role default. The explicit schema-version-3 release procedure preserves data and gates older binaries; package voice55, Comms private15, database7 and owned schema-upgrade5 tests pass. Aggregate validation, production migration, live media and cutover remain separate evidence requirements. |
| `community-client-write-failure-phases` | unverified | Client BAN and update now preserve the source commit phases on the existing pool: completed membership/unlike/analytics stages survive a later ban/request failure, while community updates precede separate places and atomic bulk acceptance. Nine actual-source PostgreSQL trigger captures independently match exactly; package community186 tests pass. Native federation and atomic join retain their separate contracts. Production crash/retry/concurrency and nonempty cutover remain unverified. |
| `community-voice-raw-cache-aliases` | known_gap | Two complete executed-source lifecycles show independent raw UUID cache keys, their original wire spellings and restart/poll behavior. Candidate stores one notification generation/scope per canonical UUID, losing that cardinality and lexical identity. Analytics spelling is already preserved; stream/cache lifecycle parity remains open. A single authoritative raw-key relation, bounded polling and data-safe migration are being reviewed before implementation. |
